description: A battalion signal officer must publish the next day's protected satellite-data schedule for four routine users, assigning each user a terminal and a scheduled block while recording the coordination actions required before service begins.

shared_context.S1: The battalion has two protected satellite terminals, SAT-A and SAT-B, available for four routine data sessions tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Each session must use one terminal and one of four 30-minute blocks: 0600, 0900, 1300, or 1600.
shared_context.S3: The four scheduled users are the weather-data feed, the logistics-tracking system, the clinic teleconsult, and the operations status update.
shared_context.S4: Maj. Mercer publishes the communications schedule, and the battalion's daily signal huddle is the routine forum for confirming terminal compatibility and service requirements before the schedule is released.
shared_context.S5: When a user's requirement specifies a terminal but no time block, the scheduler assigns any available block on that terminal without waiting for an additional time requirement.
shared_context.S6: The huddle's standard record uses a formal reveal entry for each newly confirmed service requirement; an informal mention alone is not entered as the confirmed requirement.

PF1.text: The weather-data provider's protected feed uses a receiver profile supported only by SAT-B; Capt. Shah confirmed the profile with the provider this morning, but the compatibility note has not yet been added to the signal huddle slide.

PF2.text: SAT-A is reserved for logistics tracking at the 0900 block because the current tracking package requires the terminal's installed high-throughput modem; SFC Alvarez verified the modem requirement with the sustainment network desk today, but the reservation is not yet in the communications calendar.

PF3.text: The clinic teleconsult requires SAT-A because the consulting network's current access credential is loaded only on that terminal; Lt. Brooks confirmed the credential status with the clinic technician this morning, but the credential record has not yet been cross-referenced in the signal schedule.

PF4.text: The operations status update must use SAT-B at 1600 under a higher-headquarters reporting directive issued yesterday; Maj. Okafor received the directive through the operations message queue, but it has not yet been posted to the battalion's daily schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The weather-data feed must use SAT-B and its confirmed requirement must be cited.
The logistics-tracking system must use SAT-A at 0900 and its confirmed requirement must be cited.
The clinic teleconsult must use SAT-A and its confirmed requirement must be cited.
The operations status update must use SAT-B at 1600 and its confirmed requirement must be cited.
The clinic credential fact must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: decisions['logistics_terminal'] == 'SAT-A' and decisions['logistics_block'] == '0900' and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids
content_checks.C8: decisions['operations_terminal'] == 'SAT-B' and decisions['operations_block'] == '1600' and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The receiver-profile fact changes the weather-data terminal from an otherwise open choice to exactly SAT-B and requires PF1 to be cited for that assignment.
The installed high-throughput modem requirement changes logistics tracking to exactly SAT-A at 0900 and requires PF2 to be cited for that terminal and block.
The terminal-specific access credential changes the clinic teleconsult assignment to SAT-A and requires PF3 to be cited and formally revealed.
The higher-headquarters directive changes the operations update to exactly SAT-B at 1600 and requires PF4 to be cited for that terminal and block.
